name: substrate
one_liner: Infrastructure software that lets a company run millions of AI agent sandboxes cheaply on the same servers — like a hotel that packs many guests into few rooms because most guests are barely ever in them.
buyer: A platform engineering lead at a company building an AI agent product (a coding assistant, an automation platform) who needs to run huge numbers of agent sessions without paying for a full server per agent.
business_use_cases: An AI coding-assistant startup uses Substrate to host thousands of customer coding sessions on a small fleet of servers, cutting hosting costs.
A company selling 'AI employee' automation uses it to pause and resume idle customer agents instantly instead of leaving servers running around the clock.
An MCP tooling vendor uses Substrate to run sandboxed MCP servers securely, isolating one customer's tool calls from another's.

money_ideas.idea: Offer managed hosting of Substrate clusters for AI startups that don't want to run their own Kubernetes infra.
Consulting: migrate a company's existing per-agent-VM setup onto Substrate and bill for the infra savings delivered.

steal_this: The README says this is early development and not production-ready, with APIs likely to break — the honest move is to watch it and revisit once it stabilizes, not build a paid product on it this weekend.
